model: Investment trust NAV compounding with distributions capitalised at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: forward NAV total return at the terminal year of the base case (Action de-rated from 18.5x to ~14.5x and growing EBITDA ~7%; rest of book ~11%; central costs -0.5%). The historical 20-27% NAV/share CAGRs are the Action re-rating era (multiple 11x -> 18.5x on 20-30% EBITDA growth) and are not extrapolable.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue (gross investment return) and EPS 3-yr CAGRs of 5.6%/4.3% diverge by more than 30% from the equity/NAV CAGRs of 20-22% because 'revenue' here is the fair-value gain, which was already very large in FY2023; NAV per share is the meaningful series. FCF CAGRs are on cash distributions (dividends + buybacks: FY2021 338m, FY2023 515m, FY2026 780m), not cash-flow-statement FCF.
historical_growth.notes: NAV/share 604p (FY2017) -> 3,030p (FY2026) -> 3,131p (Q1 FY2027). Total return on opening NAV: FY2017 36%, FY2018 24%, FY2019 18%, FY2020 3%, FY2021 22%, FY2022 44%, FY2023 36%, FY2024 23%, FY2025 25%, FY2026 22% (incl. +GBP 809m FX); Q1 FY2027 3% for the quarter after -GBP 276m FX. Dividends/closing NAV: FY2024 2.93%, FY2025 2.87%, FY2026 2.79%.

scenario_narratives.base: Action remains an excellent retailer but a maturing one: EBITDA growth decelerates from 13% to ~7% as the European store base passes 6,000 and LFL settles at 3-4%, and the 18.5x run-rate multiple that 3i marks it at (versus a 13x PE-ex-Action average and 7-12x for listed discounters) compresses to ~14.5x over eight years. Leverage (2.7x) and a ~3% cash yield still gear that into ~10% equity returns, so group NAV total return runs 13.5% in year one and settles at 9.5%, just under the 10% cost of equity. 3i pays out ~2.85% of NAV a year plus the GBP 495m balance of the current buyback. Base IV ~2,900p (0.94x NAV; 21% above the price).
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2022-26 run continues: Action's 400-stores-a-year roll-out and the US entry (first store 2027/28, ~100 by 2030) sustain 12-14% EBITDA growth into the 2030s, the multiple holds near 17-18.5x, and the rest of the book earns its 12-15% underwriting returns. Group NAV compounds at 16.5% falling to 10.5%, in line with what 3i actually delivered ex-FX in FY2025-Q1 FY2027. The discount closes and the market pays a 10% premium to NAV at exit, as it did through 2021-25. Bull IV ~4,200p.
scenario_narratives.bear: The May 2026 sell-off was right: LFL growth that slipped from 10.3% (2024) to 3.6% (H1 2026) keeps falling, France goes negative, the US launch burns capital, and Action's EBITDA growth drops to mid-single digits. The self-marked 18.5x multiple is cut to ~12x over three years, taking a third off Action's equity value and ~26% off group NAV; realisations elsewhere stall. NAV goes sideways for three years then compounds at 7.5%, below the cost of equity, so the trust settles at ~0.55x NAV. Bear IV ~1,400p, a 42% loss from here.

valuation_philosophy.summary: 3i is valued as what it is: a permanent-capital investment trust whose worth is the net asset value it compounds and the share of that it distributes. The NAV is taken as published (3,083p ex-dividend at 30 June 2026), the distribution stream (2.85% of NAV, plus the live buyback) is capitalised at a 10% GBP cost of equity, and the exit is the Gordon value of that stream at the retained-NAV growth rate, capped at a scenario P/NAV ceiling. The whole debate is Action: 77% of NAV, marked at 18.5x run-rate EBITDA, growing 13% but with LFL halved since 2024. Base case assumes gradual de-rating to ~14.5x; the 22% discount to NAV in the price is roughly what that de-rating is worth, so the stock is modestly cheap on a probability-weighted basis but not a bargain, and the 15% hurdle is not met at any price above ~1,200p.
key_risks_to_valuation: Action's valuation multiple: 1.0x on 18.5x moves 3i's NAV by ~GBP 1.5bn (~150p/share); the base case's 8-year glide to 14.5x could happen in one results day
Action LFL trajectory: 10.3% (2024) -> 4.9% (2025) -> 3.6% (H1 2026); France is the largest market and the weakest
US entry execution 2027-2030 (EUR 350-400m) in a market where Lidl stalled and Dollar General/Dollar Tree dominate

Gordon knife-edge: the exit P/NAV is yield / (CoE - g) with a 3.5pp spread in the base case; a 1pp change in terminal NAV return moves the exit from 0.87x to ~0.7x or 1.1x (the cap) -- see the sensitivity grid
Cost of equity: 10% on a trust that until 2026 compounded at 20%+; 11% would take ~15% off every scenario
Timing: base NAV is 30 June 2026; the H1 FY2027 results (November 2026) will restate NAV, the multiple and the buyback progress
FX: ~82% of NAV in EUR/USD, un-hedged in this model

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, LSE regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1,825-4,497p
data_sources.financials: III.L_Metrics.csv (financial-parser, GBP millions, FY2017-FY2026 + Q1 FY2027); FY2026 Annual Report (note 8 diluted NAV 30.30, Action valuation page 30, dividends note 9); Q1 FY2027 performance update 23 July 2026 (NAV 3,131p, 1,009m diluted shares, net debt GBP 481m, Action GBP 24,249m at 18.5x on EUR 2,730m run-rate EBITDA, buyback progress)
data_sources.qualitative: III.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): Action concentration, LFL deceleration, US entry, buyback, NAV discount dynamics

inputs.base_revenue_note: NOT revenue. Diluted net assets at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 update): 3,131p x 1,009m diluted shares = GBP 31,592m, less the GBP 480m (48.0p) second FY2026 dividend paid 24 July 2026 = GBP 31,112m (3,083p/share). The ex-dividend NAV is the right comparator because the market price is already ex that dividend. 3i's FY2026 revenue line (GBP 5,496m gross investment return) is a fair-value movement, not an operating flow, and is not used.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,009m diluted shares at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 update note 2, after cancelling c.11.3m shares under the buyback). Held FLAT: the remainder of the GBP 750m buyback (~GBP 495m from 1 July 2026) is modelled as a year-1 cash distribution to the flat shareholder base rather than as a falling count, which is value-neutral except that it forgoes the ~0.5% NAV/share accretion of repurchasing at 0.78x NAV. Dilutive share awards are already inside the diluted NAV figure, so SBC is not charged a second time. Count had fallen to ~1,005.6m by 21 July 2026 and should reach ~990m by December 2026.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO deliberately. The flow being capitalised is a post-interest distribution to shareholders and the base is net assets, which already deducts 3i's borrowings (net debt GBP 481m, gearing 2% at 30 June 2026). Subtracting it again would double-count. total_debt and cash below are informational anchors only.
inputs.total_debt_note: Gross borrowings at 31 March 2026 (FY2026 AR); the Q1 update gives only net debt GBP 481m and gross cash GBP 724m, implying gross borrowings ~GBP 1,205m.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Modelled flow = cash distributions to shareholders in FY2026: dividends paid GBP 765m + share repurchases GBP 15m. Owner-FCF identity (reported - SBC - interest income) does not apply on this route: an investment trust's cash-flow-statement FCF (GBP 997m, retained as reported_fcf) is realisation timing, not an owner flow.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR statement of changes in equity, share-based payments GBP 12m (FY2025: 16m). Not deducted from the flow: at 0.04% of NAV it is immaterial and the diluted NAV per share already absorbs the dilutive awards (charging it in the flow as well would double-count). House and street bases therefore coincide; band_position is null.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 financing-activity repurchases GBP 15m. The GBP 750m programme announced 14 May 2026 had spent GBP 255m (11.3m shares) by 30 June 2026 and GBP 344m (14.7m shares) by 21 July 2026; the ~GBP 495m balance from 1 July is in the year-1 distribution.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and NAV in GBP; LSE quote in pence (GBp). fx_rate 100 converts GBP/share to pence/share; no exchange-rate risk in the bridge. Underlying NAV is ~82% EUR/USD exposed (a 1% EUR move = ~GBP 248m of total return); FX is treated as zero-expected noise and not modelled.
inputs.fy0: Q1 FY2027 (NAV at 30 June 2026, ex the July 2026 dividend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, GBP-denominated: UK 10-year gilt ~4.6% (Oct 2026) + 5.0% equity risk premium x beta ~1.1 (listed private-equity trust with low parent gearing but a 77% position in a leveraged retailer) = ~10.1%, rounded to 10.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios; risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not a per-scenario discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: 3i's own lease liabilities (~GBP 20m) sit inside net assets; portfolio-company leases are inside the portfolio valuations.
inputs.nci_treatment: Not applicable: NAV is attributable to 3i shareholders; the 34.6% of Action not owned by 3i is simply not in NAV.
inputs.notes: MODEL: NAV compounding + exit discount, capitalised at the cost of equity (SKILL.md routing row 'LIC, investment trust, closed-end fund'). 3i is an investment trust whose value is its portfolio NAV (77% a single self-marked private asset, Action, valued at 18.5x run-rate EBITDA); its income statement is fair-value movement and its cash flow is realisation timing, so an owner-FCF DCF would be meaningless. ENGINE MAPPING (the dashboard sliders carry owner-FCF labels; read them as follows): 'revenue' = net assets (GBP m); 'revenue growth' = growth in NAV per share net of distributions, derived each year as (1 + NAV total return) / (1 + distribution yield) - 1; 'EBITDA margin' = cash distributions (dividends + buybacks) as % of closing NAV (3i has paid 2.8-2.9% of closing NAV as dividends in each of FY2024-26; year 1 adds the ~GBP 495m balance of the buyback); SBC, D&A, capex, working capital and cash tax are all zero (investment-trust status: capital gains exempt, cash tax GBP 0-3m/yr); 'WACC' = cost of equity 10%; 'terminal growth' = perpetual retained-NAV growth = terminal NAV total return less the distribution yield (base 6.5% = 9.5% total return - 2.85% paid out), so the Gordon value of the distribution stream is the economically consistent exit: P/NAV = yield / (CoE - g) = 0.87x in the base case; 'terminal cap multiple' = exit P/NAV ceiling / distribution yield (base 0.90x NAV = 31.6x the terminal distribution; bull 1.10x = 38.6x; bear 0.70x = 22.6x). The high-looking terminal growth figures are NOT revenue growth: dragging the slider to a conventional 2-3% would value 3i as if it stopped compounding retained capital, which is not a scenario. TIMING: the base is the 30 June 2026 NAV discounted a full year for year 1; the valuation date is 3.3 months later, so values are ~2.5% conservative on timing. SANITY: price 2,402p is 0.78x ex-dividend NAV of 3,083p; base IV implies ~0.94x, bull 1.37x, bear 0.45x.

bear.growth_rates_note: NAV total return 0.5, -2.0, -3.5, 8.0, 8.0, 7.5, 7.5, 7.5, 7.5, 7.5%. Action's LFL turns negative in France, store growth slows, the US entry absorbs capital, EBITDA growth drops to 8% -> 5%, and 3i (or the market) takes the multiple from 18.5x to ~12x over three years (-35% on Action equity, roughly -26% on group NAV before growth). Rest of book 8% with slow realisations. Dividend held in pounds under the 'maintain or grow' policy, so the yield on a shrunken NAV rises to 3.0-3.1%.
bear.terminal_growth_note: Terminal total return 7.5% less 3.1% yield. Gordon exit = 3.1% / (10% - 4.3%) = 0.54x NAV, binding below the 0.70x cap: a trust earning less than its cost of equity in perpetuity is worth less than book, consistent with the 0.5-0.6x troughs of 2009 and 2012.

base.growth_rates_note: Retained NAV growth from a NAV total-return path of 13.5, 12.0, 11.0, 10.5, 10.0, 9.5, 9.5, 9.5, 9.5, 9.5% (year 1: (1.135 / 1.0431) - 1 with the buyback in the year-1 payout; later years: (1 + TR) / 1.0285 - 1). Action (77% of NAV): EBITDA growth 13% -> 7% (store roll-out 400/yr on 3,400 with LFL 3-4%), multiple 18.5x -> ~14.5x over eight years (~-3.5%/yr equity drag), leverage held at 2.7x so EV growth gears 1.17x into equity, plus ~3% cash yield from Action dividends/recaps. Rest of book ~11% (PE ex-Action 13x avg multiple, 3iN 8-10% target), central costs and 2% gearing -0.5%.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Distributions as % of closing NAV. 2.85% = dividend policy 'maintain or grow DPS' at the FY2024-26 average payout; year 1 adds the ~GBP 495m buyback balance (1.46% of year-1 NAV).
base.terminal_growth_note: Perpetual retained-NAV growth: terminal total return 9.5% less the 2.85% distribution yield. Gordon exit = 2.85% / (10% - 6.5%) = 0.87x NAV, which binds below the 0.90x cap.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_note: 0.90x NAV ceiling / 2.85% yield. 3i traded between ~0.7x and 1.5x NAV over 2013-2026 (premium through 2021-25, 0.78x now); 0.90x assumes a persistent modest discount for single-asset concentration and a self-marked valuation.

bull.growth_rates_note: NAV total return 16.5, 15.5, 14.5, 14.0, 13.0, 12.0, 11.5, 11.0, 10.5, 10.5%. Action EBITDA growth 14% -> 7% with the US entry (2027/28, ~100 stores by 2030) working and European white space (~4,650 sites) delivering; multiple only drifts 18.5x -> 17x; rest of book at the 12-15% PE underwriting level. Close to the ex-FX run-rate 3i has actually delivered in FY2025-Q1 FY2027 (16-18%) at a constant multiple.
bull.terminal_growth_note: Terminal total return 11% less 2.85% yield. Gordon (52x) exceeds the cap, so the 1.10x NAV ceiling binds: the bull case does not pay more than a 10% premium to NAV at exit.
bull.terminal_cap_multiple_note: 1.10x NAV / 2.85% yield. 3i's average rating through the 2021-2025 compounding years; the premium has been as high as 1.5x.

entry_price.method: Price at which the projected distributions plus the year-10 exit value (Gordon on the terminal distribution rebuilt at 15%, re-capped at the scenario's P/NAV ceiling) return a 15% IRR. For a ~9.5%-return asset this lands at roughly 0.4x NAV, well below intrinsic value -- the same honest output AFI.NZ produced and not something to 'fix'.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 31.6x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because 77% of NAV is one private company valued on a multiple 3i sets itself; a de-rating of that multiple is a single decision, not a chain of events. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right (Action sustaining double-digit EBITDA growth through a US entry AND the market re-rating the trust to a premium) at a time when LFL growth has halved in two years. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
